newsitem.title: JORDAN: Amman shares close steady in selective trade.
newsitem.headline: Amman shares close steady in selective trade.

text.p: Jordan shares ended steady on Monday in local and foreign-inspired buying of selected blue-chip industrials, dealers said.
The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index shed 0.02 percent to 163.97 points in turnover worth 629,877 dinars ($888,401).
Brokers said the bourse continued to be buttressed by some orders on leading industrial and drug firms which performed well during the first half of 1997.

National Chlorine was the day's busiest traded stock in turnover worth 157,358 dinars which was rumoured to be a block sale executed by a local broker on behalf of foreign funds. It shed 0.03 dinars to 1.54 dinars.
A blue-chip firm, Arab Pharmaceutical Manufacturing which has been underpinned by favourable half-year results and good orders to Iraq, rose 0.01 dinars to 4.15 dinars in trade worth 43,123 dinars.
Jordan Cement Factory, which has been a focus of foreign fund interest over the last few months, was also unchanged at 3.97 dinars in low volume worth only 57,418 dinars.
Irbid Electricity, Jordan's second largest electricity distribution firm, rose to the maximum daily five percent limit, gaining 0.09 dinars to 1.79 dinars.

Interest in the rarely traded utility firm was sparked by an announcement last week by the government, a major shareholder in the firm, that it was looking for investors to link up with a local partner to buy up 51 percent of the company.
Overall 14 shares rose and 13 fell, with another 14 trading but closing unchanged.

The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance, fixed at 100 points at the end of 1994, was unchanged at 80.51 points, 3.46 percent down since the start of the year.
